_comment: GQuay runner overlay. The Router renders this per session into
data/sessions/<work-item>/settings.json, substituting ${...} placeholders,
and passes it with --settings. It is generated per session rather than
shared because the work item key and the inbox path differ per session.
Do not hand-edit the generated copy — edit this template.
merge_pull_request is left in an ask-by-default permission so a dead Hook
Bus degrades to 'no merge' rather than 'free merge'. A PreToolUse hook
that times out does NOT block the call — it continues through the normal
permission flow — so the gate needs this floor underneath it.
It is deliberately NOT in a deny rule: a hook returning 'allow' cannot
loosen a deny that came from settings, and that would kill the
'merge when asked' path entirely.

hooks._comment: http, not mcp_tool: SessionStart typically fires before MCP servers finish connecting.

_comment: This is the park loop, and it is structural on purpose. An agent that
*forgets* to call await_events ends its turn and the session dies with
work outstanding, and 'remember to call the tool' is exactly the kind of
instruction that survives twenty turns and then does not.
The tool's timeout_s is set below this hook's timeout so the server
returns 'nothing arrived' first and the turn ends deliberately. If the
hook itself times out, Claude Code cancels it and discards the output,
so no decision is rendered and the turn ends anyway — the failure mode
is 'session parks', not 'session hangs'.

hooks._comment: PreToolUse fires before any permission-mode check, so this deny holds even under bypassPermissions.
agent-locks is advisory by design. This turns an overlap report into a permission decision.

_comment: async because a Teams post must never sit in front of the agent's next turn.
This is also where the linking rule lands: a create_pull_request response
gives the Router the PR number, and one session then owns both threads.
MCP tools match as mcp__<server>__<tool>; a whole-server match needs the
'.*' suffix, since a bare prefix is compared as an exact string.
Mid-task delivery. An agent parked in await_events is reachable through
the MCP call; an agent three files into a refactor is not. This reads the
work item's inbox file and, if a message is waiting, prints it to stderr
and exits 2 — which wakes Claude and surfaces it as a system reminder
without a restart.

hooks._comment: Notification output and exit code are ignored — a pure observation point, which is what is wanted.
Compaction eventually destroys the oldest context, and the oldest context here is the issue itself.

_comment: PreModelSwitch can block a switch, and unlike other events a hook
cancelled at its timeout *blocks* the switch — so it fails closed by
default. The Router resolves the model at spawn from labels; drifting
mid-session would make the audit line in the transcript a lie.

hooks._comment: Locks have no TTL; without this a crashed agent holds its claim forever.
